metadata.methods_description: Participants sat in a darkened, sound-attenuated room viewing a 24in LCD monitor at 60in distance. They were presented with 90 four-letter real words and 90 four-letter pseudowords in three flanker conditions (no flanker, identical flankers, different flankers), totaling 270 trials. Each trial began with a purple fixation cross (1000ms), followed by a white fixation cross (500ms), then the stimulus (150ms), followed by a blank screen until the participant responded via a game controller.

citation_details.title: Trial-history modulation in orthographic flanker lexical decision: code and aggregate reproducibility package
citation_details.author: guo
citation_details.abstract: Code, aggregate results, figures, analysis-governance records, and supplementary audit materials for a secondary analysis of the public OpenNeuro Flankers-NEAR (ds005866 v1.0.1) and Flankers-FAR (ds005868 v1.0.1) datasets. Version 1.1.0 documents the internally dated, nonregistered 103-record analysis; the post hoc 108-record behavior-complete analysis; dual covariance assumptions; exact-predecessor correction; ratio-of-ratios and equal-context estimands; common-support, template, boundary, accuracy, and 3 × 3 diagnostics; and a full EEG unit, rejection-threshold, feature, and waveform audit. Raw and participant-level data are not redistributed.

citation_details.title: Analyzing neural response to visual stimuli: Firing rates, frequency band dynamics, and synchrony in near and far flanker conditions
citation_details.author: Manjeet Kunwar, Nabin Bhusal, Niraj Dhital
citation_details.abstract: The present work investigates how spatial configurations of distractor stimuli influence neural processing during visual perception, specifically contrasting Near and Far flanker conditions. Electroencephalography (EEG) recordings of 50 people were obtained from an online open-access database called OpenNeuro and evenly assigned to each condition. A multimodal analytical approach was employed, incorporating spectrogram analysis, wavelet transformation, time-frequency decomposition, and cross-correlation to comprehensively characterize neural activity. Inferred neural firing rates were examined to assess differences in cognitive engagement. Results indicate that the Near flanker condition elicited increased delta and theta band power in frontal regions and higher estimated firing rates, suggesting elevated cognitive load and attentional demands. In contrast, the Far condition exhibited greater alpha and beta activity, consistent with more efficient neural processing. Despite these trends, statistical analysis revealed no significant difference in firing rates between the two conditions (p = 0.735). These findings highlight the impact of spatial context on attentional modulation and underscore the utility of EEG-based measures for probing the neural mechanisms underlying visual cognition.

citation_details.title: Identity-disjoint cross-context prediction of lexical-decision latency from single-trial EEG
citation_details.author: guo
citation_details.abstract: Code and aggregate reproducibility package for the manuscript. Includes the frozen analysis specification, signal and model scripts, complementary sensitivity-analysis code, aggregate results, figures, and provenance records. Source data: OpenNeuro ds005866 v1.0.1 and ds005868 v1.0.1. Excludes raw EEG, behavioral rows, trial-level predictions, feature matrices, and participant-level identity linkage.
